place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 大比 · 对秦雁
place.en: Chending Temple · The contest · Against Qin Yan

setup.zh: 再上台，对面是名册上排头一个的秦雁：真灵根，六层，剑在背上。她冲你一抱拳：「沈师弟，听说你只有二层。」
setup.en: Back on the stage, facing the one first on the register, Qin Yan: true root, layer six, a sword on her back. She salutes you: "Brother Shen, I hear you're only at layer two."

recap.zh: 你躲了秦雁三十一剑，一剑也没还；她踩着石缝退出了台子，压低声音说：「藏得好。」袖子里那张雷符，她始终没掏。
recap.en: You dodged thirty-one of Qin Yan's thrusts and never struck back; she stepped in the crack and went off the stage, and said low: "Well hidden." The thunder talisman in her sleeve she never drew.

zh: 名册上排头一个：秦雁，六层。
三十一剑。你只看她的脚。
en: First on the register: Qin Yan, layer six.
Thirty-one thrusts. You watch only her feet.

story.zh: 她上台的时候，冲小满抱了抱拳：「沈师弟，听说你只有二层。」小满也抱了抱拳：「是。」秦雁道：「那我让你三招。」小满道：「师姐不用让。我打不过，会跑的。」秦雁一愣，随即笑了。
story.en: Coming up onto the stage she saluted Xiaoman: "Brother Shen, I hear you're only at layer two." Xiaoman saluted back: "Yes." "Then I'll give you three moves." "No need, sister. If I can't win, I'll run." Qin Yan was startled, then laughed.

exits.means: fights Qin Yan by dodging, never striking back

withdrawn.zh: 秦雁收了剑，退后一步：「再来。」
withdrawn.en: Qin Yan sheathes her sword and steps back. "Again."

story.zh:
这一场，跟孙二狗那一场大不一样。秦雁的剑是真剑，招是真招，一剑一剑递过来，又快又稳，逼得台下的人屏住了气。说书先生讲过一门剑法，专看对手出手之前的那一下，叫「料敌机先」。他爹在黑松岭的山涧边上讲得更土：天下的鹿，都是先动脚。小满不看她的剑，看她的脚：剑往哪里去，脚先往哪里挪；脚往哪里挪，肩膀先往哪里沉。剑再快，他只看她的脚。他躲得很难看，东一跳，西一滚，有两回简直是连滚带爬，引得台下一阵一阵地笑。可笑着笑着，便有人觉出不对来了：三十招过去，那口剑一回也没碰着他。

有一剑来得太快，他来不及看脚，只得往后一仰，剑尖贴着他的鼻子过去，削下了他额前的一绺头发。那绺头发在半空里飘啊飘，飘到台下，正落在阿禾的小本子上。阿禾低头看了一眼，把它夹进了本子里，面无表情，记了一笔。

到第三十一招，秦雁一剑刺空，脚下踩到了五行台边上那道长草的石缝，身子晃了一晃。小满便在这时伸手，在她手腕上轻轻一带——只是一带，像拉住一个要摔倒的人——她便顺着自己那一剑的劲儿，一步一步，退出了台子。执事敲锣：「沈小满，胜。」台下又是一片寂静，跟着便有人叫起来：「运气！」「石缝！她踩着石缝了！」

执事翻开名册，提起笔，在排头那一行「秦雁」两个字上，画了一道。三年的队，一笔。台下有人叹了口气。人堆里一个嗓子，又尖又哑：「你……你把她打下去了？」是孙二狗。他脸色发白，指着台下那个淡蓝衣裳的背影，「秘境里，拿剑鞘把我从坑里拽上来的，就是她。半块干粮，也是她给的。」

小满站在台上，张了张嘴，一句话也答不上来。他赢了。他赢的这一场，是拿一个人的三年换的。

老槐树底下，钱掌柜拿炭条在木板上添了一行：**决赛　马小宝　一赔一。**又在底下写了个「沈」字，写了一半，停住了，想了想，把炭条一搁，在那半个字后头画了一道杠——不收了。有人问他怎么不收，他拨着算盘道：「看不准的，不开。」

秦雁站在台下，低头看了看自己的手腕，又抬起头来看小满，看了好一会儿。她走到台边，冲他抱了一抱拳，压低了声音：「藏得好。」小满也冲她抱了一抱拳：「师姐也是。」秦雁的眉毛轻轻一挑。她右手的袖子里，一直扣着一张黄纸符，从第一招扣到第三十一招，始终没有掏出来。小满看见了袖口里露出来的那一角，她也知道他看见了。

秦雁道：「雷符。我娘留给我的，就这一张。掏出来，五行台要炸去半边。」她朝台下看了一眼，头一排蹲着几个刚进门的小孩子，正张着嘴看她，「我不是让你。我是没法掏。」她顿了一顿，又道：「你那两步，是猎户的步子吧？」小满一怔：「师姐怎么知道？」秦雁道：「我爹也是打猎的。我这个名字，就是他起的——他说雁是天上最难射的东西，一辈子没射着过一只。」

她转身要走，又停住了，背对着他，声音压得更低：「昨天夜里，马小宝在你们屋里拿那面镜子照了一圈，今天一早，满外门都传遍了：照到沈小满，沈小满翻了个身。」她没有回头，「决赛在日落。你怀里揣着的，不管是什么，捂紧了。」
story.en:
This bout was nothing like Sun Ergou's. Qin Yan's sword was a real sword, her moves real moves, thrust after thrust, fast and steady, till the crowd held its breath. The storytellers told of a swordsmanship that watches for the instant before the opponent moves — reading the enemy before he strikes. His father, by the stream at Black Pine Ridge, put it plainer: every deer under heaven moves its feet first. Xiaoman didn't watch her sword; he watched her feet: wherever the sword was going, the foot moved first; wherever the foot moved, the shoulder dipped first. However fast the sword, he watched her feet. He dodged very badly — a hop here, a roll there, twice practically scrambling on all fours — and the crowd laughed wave after wave. But laughing, some began to sense something wrong: thirty moves gone, and that sword hadn't touched him once.

One thrust came too fast to read her feet; he could only fling himself back, and the point went past the tip of his nose and sheared off a lock of hair from his forehead. The lock floated down and down, off the stage, and landed right on A He's notebook. She glanced at it, tucked it between the pages, and, deadpan, made a note.

At the thirty-first move Qin Yan's thrust met air, and her foot came down on the grassy crack at the edge of the platform; she wavered. Just then Xiaoman put out a hand and drew lightly on her wrist — only drew, like catching someone about to fall — and she went with her own thrust, step by step, right off the stage. The steward struck the gong: "Shen Xiaoman wins." Silence again below, then shouts: "Luck!" "The crack! She stepped in the crack!"

The steward opened the register, took up his brush, and drew one stroke through the name Qin Yan on the top line. Three years of queuing: one stroke. Someone below sighed. From the crowd a shrill, hoarse voice: "You… you knocked her down?" It was Sun Ergou, white in the face, pointing at the pale-blue back below the stage. "In the hidden realm — the one who pulled me out of the pit with her scabbard, that was her. The half ration, that was her too."

Xiaoman stood on the stage and opened his mouth and couldn't answer a word. He had won. And what he'd won it with was someone's three years.

Under the pagoda tree Money-Keeper Qian added a line to the board in charcoal: **Final — Ma Xiaobao, one to one.** Below it he wrote half the character Shen, stopped, thought, put down the charcoal and drew a stroke through the half-character — not taking bets. Someone asked why. Clicking his abacus: "What I can't call, I don't open."

Below the stage Qin Yan looked down at her wrist, then up at Xiaoman, a long while. She came to the edge, saluted him, and said low: "Well hidden." Xiaoman saluted back: "You too, sister." Her eyebrow lifted slightly. In her right sleeve, all along, she had held a yellow paper talisman, from the first move to the thirty-first, and never drawn it. Xiaoman had seen the corner peeping from her cuff, and she knew he'd seen.

"A thunder talisman," said Qin Yan. "My mother left it to me, just the one. Draw it, and half the platform goes up." She glanced below: in the front row crouched a few new little ones, mouths open, watching her. "I wasn't letting you win. I couldn't draw it." She paused. "Those steps of yours — hunter's steps, aren't they?" Xiaoman started. "How do you know, sister?" "My father hunts too. He gave me my name — he said the wild goose is the hardest thing in the sky to shoot; he never hit one in his life."

She turned to go, then stopped with her back to him and spoke lower still: "Last night Ma Xiaobao swept that mirror round your room, and by this morning the whole outer court knew: when it reached Shen Xiaoman, Shen Xiaoman rolled over." She didn't turn. "The final's at sunset. Whatever you've got in your coat, hold it tight."
